### The data channel

Timed inside the page, median of the repeats. The burst row is the longest gap between two animation frames while the page sends a burst and the app handles it; the row under it is the same measurement with no burst, which is what one frame is on this machine. ### Whose cost: interpreter, Textual, or channel

The same workloads, timed from inside Python, in every runtime. The loop touches nothing but the interpreter, so the ratio between its native and browser columns is what the interpreter costs; a workload whose ratio matches it is slow because of the interpreter rather than anything on top. Milliseconds, median.

|  | chromium main | chromium worker | firefox main | firefox worker | native |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pure-Python loop, 3,000,000 iterations | 142 | 143 | 164 | 159 | 97.47 |

| mount and remove 200 widgets | 50.90 | 53.40 | 114 | 116 | 16.62 |

### Leaks

A workload repeated in rounds, with memory read after each from every vantage point and a full collection first. Growth that continues into the second half is a leak, and the row it shows in says whose: Python objects are Python, the JS heap is the page, PSS is everything including the interpreter's linear memory.

**Messages**: 10 rounds of 5,000 messages through the channel.
